question: What is the main job of the Theatre Sterile Supply Unit (TSSU)?

options.A: Disposing of hospital general waste materials
options.C: Purchasing new hospital furniture and office supplies
options.D: Administering anesthesia inside the operating room

explanation: You got this! The TSSU is the heartbeat behind every safe surgery, making sure all medical instruments are properly cleaned, sterilized, and ready for use. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is the TSSU so important for safe nursing practice?

options.A: It reduces the duration of complex operations in theatre
options.B: It ensures patients sleep comfortably before receiving anesthesia
options.C: It lowers the financial cost of purchasing surgical equipment
options.D: It prevents the transmission of infectious agents during surgery

explanation: Spot on! By providing truly sterile instruments, the TSSU protects surgical patients from picking up nasty post-op infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: When dirty instruments arrive from the operating theatre, which zone of the TSSU do they enter first?
explanation: Exactly! Dirty items always go straight to the decontamination zone first so they can be safely washed and cleaned. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the main reason for using directional airflow inside the TSSU layout?

options.A: Drying wet surgical instruments faster after washing
options.B: Preventing airborne contaminants from moving into clean areas
options.C: Reducing the electrical energy consumption of the building
options.D: Keeping the room temperature comfortable for working staff

explanation: Well done! Airflow control uses air pressure to make sure dirty air never blows into the clean packing or storage areas. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: What must be done to surgical instruments before they go into the autoclave for sterilization?

options.C: Immediate packaging in heavy canvas bags

explanation: You got it! You can't sterilize dirt. Instruments must be thoroughly washed and cleared of all organic matter first. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why should surgical instruments be kept moist right after a surgery?

options.A: To cool down the metal items after exposure to body heat
options.B: To start the chemical sterilization process inside the theatre
options.C: To make the instruments heavier for accurate inventory counting
options.D: To prevent blood and tissue from drying onto the metal surfaces

explanation: Spot on! Once blood dries up on metal, it becomes super stubborn to remove and can ruin fine instruments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: Where should you place a chemical indicator strip when packing surgical instrument sets?

options.A: Attached to the uniform of the floor nurse
options.B: Inside the instrument tray or pack
options.C: Inside the office logbook of the supervisor
options.D: On the outer storage shelf of the room

explanation: Correct! Putting the indicator right inside the pack lets you check if the sterilizing steam or gas actually reached the instruments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why do nurses or techs inspect instruments with a magnifying glass before packing them?

options.A: To detect hidden residual soil or microscopic structural damage
options.B: To polish the stainless steel to a shiny finish
options.C: To count the exact number of pieces in the tray
options.D: To read the serial numbers printed by the manufacturer

explanation: Well done! A magnifying glass helps catch tiny cracks or leftover dirt that our normal eyes might easily miss. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which organism is commonly used as a biological indicator to test steam autoclaves?
explanation: You got it! These heat-resistant spores are tough cookies, making them the gold standard for testing if an autoclave is truly killing all microbes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: When would a hospital choose ethylene oxide gas sterilization instead of a standard steam autoclave?

options.A: For routine stainless steel scissors and heavy orthopedic hammers
options.B: When surgical trays need to be processed in under twenty minutes
options.C: When the hospital runs out of standard chemical indicator strips
options.D: For instruments that are sensitive to high heat and moisture

explanation: Spot on! Ethylene oxide works at lower temperatures, which is a lifesaver for delicate tools that would melt or get ruined in regular steam heat. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which inventory rule makes sure that older sterile packs are used up before newer ones?
explanation: Correct! FIFO stock rotation keeps supplies moving so nothing sits on the shelf past its expiry date. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: What should you do if you notice a sterile pack has a torn wrapper on the shelf?

options.A: Place adhesive tape over the tear and store it back on the shelf
options.B: Send it straight to the operating theatre for immediate use
options.C: Wipe the outside wrapper with alcohol and leave it in place
options.D: Send the item back to the TSSU for complete reprocessing

explanation: You got it! Once a wrapper is torn, the sterile barrier is broken. Never trust it—send it back to be re-sterilized. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which personal protective gear is most important when working in the TSSU decontamination area?

options.A: Patient isolation mask with oxygen tubing
options.B: Reflective safety vest and hard hat
options.D: Sterile surgical gown and latex gloves

explanation: Spot on! Since you are washing dirty instruments, a waterproof apron and sturdy utility gloves protect you from splashes and harsh wash chemicals. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why do staff members wear hair covers and masks in the clean packing zone of the TSSU?

options.A: To comply with fire safety regulations inside hospital corridors
options.B: To prevent human skin scales and hair from contaminating sterile packs
options.C: To protect the workers from breathing in harsh steam from autoclaves
options.D: To keep the staff warm during cold morning shifts in the basement

explanation: Well done! Hair and shedding skin cells carry bacteria, so covering up keeps our freshly cleaned surgical tools safe from accidental contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)
